messages:
alina: Heads-up design review: the new version-history timeline shows per-snapshot CTAs inline (Rollback / Promote). Users report accidental clicks and screen reader confusion. Want to iterate on discovery, copy, and a11y.

jon: Noted. My first thought is to demote destructive actions into an overflow menu and make the primary inline button non-destructive (e.g., 'Open revert preview'). That keeps the path short for common flows but avoids one-click nukes.

miriam: Accessibility: inline buttons must include context in the accessible name. For example: aria-label="Open revert preview for version v2.1.3 deployed Mar 8, affects service payments." This prevents ambiguous UI for screen-reader users. Also ensure dialog announces the exact commit sha being reverted.

sam: UX: can we expose an inline "quick details" on hover/focus instead of full modal? Keyboard users should still get the same content via focus. Maybe use a popover with a clear 'Apply revert' and 'More options' link that opens overflow.

hannah: Visual: overlapping canary bands are hard to tell apart at small widths. I propose adding texture/hatching plus an outline stroke for each variant so high-contrast mode and monochrome prints are readable. Also add a micro legend that can be toggled.

jon: CSS snippet idea for patterns (high-contrast fallback):

```css
.variant-a { background-image: repeating-linear-gradient(45deg, rgba(0,0,0,0.04) 0 6px, transparent 6px 12px); }
.variant-b { background-image: repeating-linear-gradient(135deg, rgba(0,0,0,0.05) 0 6px, transparent 6px 12px); }
.variant-c { background-image: repeating-linear-gradient(90deg, rgba(0,0,0,0.03) 0 4px, transparent 4px 8px); }
```

miriam: Make sure focus outline sits above the pattern. Use a 3px solid token from the high-contrast palette and add outline-offset so it's not clipped. Also avoid relying on color alone to convey variant meaning.

alina: Copy adjustments: current inline label 'Rollback' reads scary. Alternatives: 'Preview revert', 'Revert (preview)', or 'Revert: preview'. For the destructive action buried in overflow, label it 'Force revert (no canary)'. Include reason text in the confirmation: who initiated, timestamp, commit sha.

sam: Undo window UX: many teams want undo but the current toast disappears too fast. Propose: show toast 'Revert started — view progress or undo (available for 30s)'. Make 'Undo' a persistent action in the timeline entry for that 30s window, and show a subtle spinner state on the snapshot.

hannah: For A/B experiments we need to show expected metric delta when previewing a revert, otherwise product managers will be surprised. Small inline metric estimates (latency, error-rate, cost) would be great. Add aria-describedby linking the preview control to that metrics summary.

miriam: Announcements & live regions: when scrubbing through versions with keyboard, speak a polite summary: 'Version v2.1.3 — deployed 2h ago — traffic 10% — preview available'. Use aria-live="polite". Avoid assertive so you don't interrupt typing.

jon: Keyboard flow: local shortcuts only. In component help: 'r = open revert preview, Shift+R = force revert (requires power-shortcuts enabled)'. Provide a settings toggle to enable power shortcuts so we don't surprise new users. Display shortcuts in a small 'keyboard' hint inside the popover.

alina: Interaction detail: kebab menu must be focusable and operate with Enter/Space. When choosing 'Force revert', show a two-step confirmation with a typed commit SHA to confirm (for extra-destructive).

sam: E2E coverage ask: add tests for keyboard navigation of the timeline, aria-live announcements, overflow menu behavior, and toast undo action. Also accessibility smoke with VoiceOver and NVDA.

devops-bot: ui-queue: keyboard-e2e + a11y-smoke tests added as job #6010. Link PR in thread when ready. :white_check_mark:

miriam: Quick checklist from thread: 1) accessible names for inline controls, 2) aria-live polite for scrubber announcements, 3) focus trap & commit details in confirmations, 4) pattern fills + visible focus outlines, 5) undo affordance in toast + timeline, 6) metrics summary linked via aria-describedby.

alina: Thanks, everyone. I'll update the figma with the 'Preview revert' primary, overflow 'Force revert' with typed SHA confirmation, patterned canary fills, and the micro-metrics in the preview. Ping me for a quick screen-reader pass once prototype is up.
